key_insight: AI-accelerated bottom-up simulations can predict the amorphous microstructure of ultra-high-molecular-weight poly(1,3-dioxolane) by resolving chain-length-dependent diffraction features into distinct monomer and polymer contributions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a first-principles route to validate and guide synthesis of recyclable UHMW polymers with targeted mechanical performance when conventional diffraction cannot reveal atomistic structure.
method: AI²-BPSP framework simulates living cationic ring-opening polymerization under experimental conditions.
Machine-learning force fields are trained against van der Waals-corrected hybrid DFT.
Predicted X-ray and neutron signals are partitioned into growing-chain and surrounding-monomer contributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports statistically significant, chain-length-resolved diffraction predictions with a monomer peak near q≈1.5 Å⁻¹ that decays as monomer is consumed and a polymer peak near q≈1.6 Å⁻¹ that grows with chain length.
watch_item: The predictions are computationally intensive and still require direct experimental validation to confirm the inferred amorphous microstructure.
paper_title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
